areas.name: Black Tusk
areas.blurb: The Black Tusk is a dark volcanic spire that stands above Garibaldi Lake and is visible from the Whistler corridor. Hikers reach its base by a long trail, and the top is a short scramble.

areas.name: Golden Hinde
areas.blurb: Golden Hinde is the highest peak on Vancouver Island, set deep in the centre of Strathcona Provincial Park far from any road. It is reached only by a multi-day trek.

routes.name: Standard Route from Rubble Creek
routes.rock_grade: Class 3 chute on the Tusk's upper rock, then a narrow ridge of loose rock; the slightly higher true summit needs a short 5th-class gap crossing and is seldom climbed
routes.best_season: Midsummer to early fall, once the approach slopes are free of snow. Wet or icy rock in the chute makes the climb much harder, and park staff discourage the final chute for those without scrambling experience.
routes.overview: A well-graded trail climbs from the Rubble Creek lot past the Taylor Meadows and Garibaldi Lake area, then leaves maintained tread on the ridge to reach the base of the Tusk. The long approach is the main effort; the climbing is a short but exposed Class 3 chute followed by a loose crest to the commonly reached top.
routes.beta: Follow the main trail up many switchbacks and across the Taylor Meadows plateau to the ridge below the Tusk, where the maintained route ends at a park sign. Continue on worn paths across loose shale that slides back with each step toward the foot of the spire. Climb the chute that splits the rock, keeping to the firmer sides and watching for loose blocks that parties below could be hit by. The chute tops out on an exposed crest of loose rock that leads to the usual summit. The marginally taller true summit lies beyond a gap that requires 5th-class moves and is rarely done.
routes.approach: The Rubble Creek parking lot sits about 3 km up a paved side road off the Sea to Sky Highway south of Whistler, at roughly 590 m. The trail begins here and gains about 1,700 m to the base of the scramble.
routes.descent_text: Reverse the chute carefully, ideally one party at a time to avoid dropping rock on those below, then follow the loose shale back to the park sign and the trail down to the lot.
routes.turnaround: Turn back if the chute is wet or snow-covered, or if you cannot be down the trail before dark; the day is long.
routes.bail: Retreat is down the same chute and shale slope, then the trail.

pitch_detail.notes: Well-graded maintained trail with a lot of switchbacks and distance, to the park sign on the ridge.
Unmaintained path over loose shale that slides underfoot.
Short chute on fairly solid rock to the crest; beware of rockfall.
Exposed ridge of loose rock to the usual top.

obj_haz: Afternoon storms on an exposed spire
routes.watch_out:
Pulling rock loose in the chute endangers anyone beneath
The shale slope slides back with each step
A long day: plan to be on the trail in daylight
pro_tips: Climb the chute one party at a time

routes.name: Phillips Ridge Route
routes.rock_grade: Class 3-4 scrambling on loose basalt and a steep snow couloir below the summit, with a Class 3 ledge on the approach ridge
routes.best_season: Late summer, when the ridge and gully are largely free of snow. Early in the season the couloir holds firm snow and ice, and parties need axes and crampons.
routes.overview: A committing multi-day trek from the Westmin Mine trailhead climbs Phillips Ridge, traverses a string of rises past alpine lakes, and descends to the basin below the north end of the summit ridge. A scree slope and a steep couloir lead to a short scramble on the top.
routes.beta: From the Westmin lot, climb switchbacks to Arnica Lake and then follow the long ridge over several bumps; a roughly 6 m Class 3 ledge near Terror Peak is the main exposure there. Descend steeply to the Carter Lake area, continue past Opal Lake and over a col to the Schjelderup lakes, then drop into the gully between the Schjelderup and Burman drainages. Cross to Moraine Lake, climb the south and southeast scree slopes toward the north end of the summit ridge, and ascend the steep couloir (roughly 55 degrees in places, with a narrow line beside the snow). A short scramble of about 50 m finishes on the summit.
routes.approach: Drive to the Westmin Mine area at the south end of Buttle Lake in Strathcona Provincial Park; the trail begins from the lot next to the old mine.
routes.descent_text: Descend the couloir or the sunny bowl to its south, return over the scree to Moraine Lake and retrace the traverse to your camp.
routes.turnaround: Turn back if the couloir snow is not firm or if rockfall is active above you; a slip here is unprotected.
routes.bail: Retreat is the way you came, over the ridge to the trailhead; there is no quick exit.

pitch_detail.notes: Switchback trail up to the ridge.
Many ups and downs; a short Class 3 ledge by Terror Peak.
Steep slippery descents and boot-path route-finding.
South and southeast scree slopes toward the north end of the summit ridge.
Steep snow in a couloir, then about 50 m of scrambling on loose basalt.

what_to_bring: Overnight camping gear for several days
hazards: Steep snow couloir with a no-fall runout
Class 3 ledge on the approach ridge
obj_haz: Fog making the route hard to follow
routes.watch_out:
Wear a helmet in the couloir
The trail can vanish in fog
The trip is multi-day and far from help
pro_tips: Carry an ice axe and crampons in early season
Plan for four or more days
